lessons: Open on a number or a contradiction in the first 2 seconds, never on a name or title card.
First scene shows the moving part, not the empty bench.
Vary the hero object each week; don't put the same cylinder in every episode.
Say only claims that two sources agree on; use ranges ('15 to 20 times') when sources differ.
End on one short line that sums it up, then one send or follow line (alternate them).
Reels viewers decide in about 1.5 s: frame 1 already shows the part moving with the key number in the caption; no slow push-in from an empty shot.
Instagram reach to non-followers follows sends per reach (ours: 0 sends on 1,061 reach): give one surprising, shareable fact and end with a send line ('Send this to someone who rides a two-stroke').
Make the last line and frame lead back into the first so the Short loops: rewatches add watch time on both platforms.

Proven hook (our best so far: 1,000 YouTube views and 1,251 Instagram views): 'Your <thing you own> <violent verb> <extreme number> times a second' ('Your engine explodes 50 times a second'). Give each episode its own object, verb and number, and use this frame in at most 4 of the 14 episodes so the batch does not look templated.
